sources: Joyce, Patrick Weston. Ancient Celtic Romances. London: Parkgate Books, 1997, 362+.

text: Ailna was an Irish heroine. When the bold warriors of the Fianna killed her husband Mergah, she set out to take revenge. Changing herself into a deer, she led the Fianna leader Fionn Mac Cumhaill and his musician companion Dáire on a desperate chase until they were exhausted. Then she wrapped them in a Druid's fog so they could not find their way home. When the Fianna heard Dáire's music and tried a rescue, they too got lost in the thick fog. Wandering, Fionn and Dáire met another lost traveler, Glanlua, who asked them for aid. Then fairy music rose from the fog, and all fell asleep. When the fog cleared, Fionn found himself on the shore of a lake. A giant and a beautiful woman rose from it, demanding payment for the murder of Mergah and the deaths of his nephews, the giant's sons. The pair were Ailna and her brother Dryantore. They imprisoned the heroes in a dungeon. Glanlua became Ailna's companion and learned from her of a magical drinking horn that would restore health and strength. When the Fianna at last located Fionn, the wily Conan slipped the vessel to him. Strengthened, Fionn broke his bonds and escaped.
objective: Record Ailna, the heroine who avenged her husband against the Fianna.
key_results: Show her shape-shifting, her fog, and the imprisonment and escape of the heroes.
